speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: All these studies have found evidence to support the gateway effect.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On Mr Leon Perera's question regarding standardised packaging, we are still studying standardised packaging.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our final decision on whether to proceed with the measure will be made only after the upcoming public consultation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The decision on whether to proceed on standardised packaging would be based on several considerations, including public health, intellectual property and international law perspectives.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will ensure that any measure, if introduced, is consistent with our domestic law and international obligations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Leon Perera has asked whether e-cigarettes are as harmful or more harmful than conventional cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The correct question should be whether e-cigarettes are harmful to health, and the answer is yes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: E-cigarettes expose users to chemicals and toxins that cause adverse health effects.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Leon Perera asked about MOH's stance on tobacco harm reduction.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We opt for high and precautionary levels of public health protection.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: While there are studies to claim that there is no gateway effect, there are as many, more authoritative, studies which point to a gateway effect.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In response to Mr Leon Perera and Mr Louis Ng's comment on other countries allowing ENDS, there is actually no consensus among public health authorities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: While the UK has advocated for e-cigarettes to have a central role in smoking cessation, the US is pushing for tighter regulation of ENDS and, in other countries, sale of ENDS remains banned.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have looked at the claim that ENDS are "95% safer than cigarettes" made in a 2015 report by Public Health England and repeated by the Royal College of Physicians.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: A number of studies used by the report were of limited quality.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In fact, an editorial in the Lancet, a leading medical journal, has criticised the report for using weak evidence.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Leon Perera cited the Cochrane Review to support the claim that e-cigarettes can help smokers to quit.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have studied the report, I have read the report, but what he did not emphasise was the report found that the overall quality of evidence that e-cigarettes can help smokers to quit is low.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The report mentioned about the small number of trials, low-event rates and wide confidence intervals.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The study concluded that the long-term safety of the use of ENDS was unknown.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I am sure Mr Leon Perera does not want to put our smokers who are trying very hard to quit at risk.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Of note also is that e-cigarettes are still not available to the UK National Health Service for Smoking Cessation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: No electronic cigarette has been licensed by the UK Medicine and Health Regulatory Agency.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is because there is no conclusive scientific evidence proving the product's safety and efficacy.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Australia, too, does not recommend ENDS until there is more evidence on safety.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And Australia also does not recommend ENDS until there is more evidence on its effectiveness in smoking cessation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Some tobacco companies are pivoting from smoke-producing cigarettes to smoke-free but nicotine-containing products, such as e-cigarettes and heat-not-burn tobacco products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: They hire researchers and lobbyists to help them with this pivot.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Smokeless, electronic, but make no mistake, the revenue-generating base product is still nicotine.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: ENDS are marketed as "healthier" alternatives and youths are targeted.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We must not let our guard down and we must protect our young.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our goal is not just a smoke-free future, but a nicotine-free one.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So-called lesser-harm tobacco products still expose the user to toxic and addictive ways that are harmful to health.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In response to Mr Leon Perera, we are open to evidence proving that ENDS are safe and effective for smoking cessation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: ENDS manufacturers, as I have mentioned earlier, can submit evidence for us to evaluate their products for registration as smoking cessation therapy under the Health Products Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: A number of Members have raised concerns on the online sales and smuggling for ENDS.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: HSA enlists the help of e-commerce sites to shut down listings for prohibited products, such as ENDS and their refill liquids and cartridges.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: ICA and Singapore Post also assist to conduct regular checks for prohibited products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if we can take action if sellers are not within our jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is a challenge because we have limited powers to act against parties located outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Persons who purchase prohibited products from overseas will be liable for an offence even if the seller is based outside Singapore.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu highlighted the possible impact of the MLA increase on retailers, in particular, how employees who are below 21 will not be allowed to handle tobacco sales.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have met with retailers and have heard their concerns.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Current employees who are above 18 will not be affected as the MLA increase would be phased in.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Thus, a small number of businesses will face challenges after the MLA is implemented.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We seek the support of the industry in supporting the MLA policy.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is to ensure we achieve our wider public health objectives.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will continue to work with tobacco retailers to ensure the smooth implementation of the MLA increase.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Ms Joan Pereira suggested that we place greater onus on logistics companies to curb the importation of prohibited products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have been reaching out to major logistics companies, as well as the Singapore Aircargo Agents Association, to educate and remind the industry of the ban on emerging and imitation tobacco products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu also asked if we can remove the ceilings for fines for sale, distribution and import of ENDS and to base the penalties on the quantity and value of the products seized.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Fines that are meted out for such offences will generally take into account the volume and potential profit that could be made.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We note Dr Chia's suggestion and will consider it when we next review the penalty framework of the Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Public education remains a key pillar of our tobacco control programme and it is vital to make the public aware of the harms of smoking, including prohibited products, such as ENDS.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: A number of Members have asked MOH to enhance our public education.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Through portals like the Health Hub as well as the Healthy Lifestyle Festival Singapore, we raise awareness among smokers on how their habit has an impact on their children and motivate them to stay smoke-free.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will continue to explore ways to improve and are reviewing our public education and outreach strategy.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Ms K Thanaletchimi highlighted the importance of stemming social supply for underage smokers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Supplying tobacco to underage persons is already an offence under the Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will look into ways to raise greater public awareness of this and to educate older family members and friends on this.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested enlisting the help of volunteers to carry out public education and enforcement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Currently, we do not deploy volunteers for enforcement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: However, we have volunteers for public education efforts, such as our "I Quit" Ambassadors.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar has expressed concern that the number of Malay smokers remains high.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: HPB holds over 200 roadshows in the community island-wide every year.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Specific to the Malay community, HPB is partnering with Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) and mosques to help Malay/Muslim smokers to quit.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The response to the "I Quit" Ramadan roadshows, held since 2012, has been encouraging.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are studying ways to expand outreach and public education efforts to all segments of the population all year round.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA monitors the trend of the sale and abuse of controlled drugs, including those mixed with tobacco, and will take the necessary enforcement action against traffickers and abusers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In response to Ms Joan Pereira's question on reducing the number of tobacco licences, we regulate where tobacco should not be sold.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These places include healthcare institutions, educational institutions and places which may disproportionately attract the young, such as gaming arcades.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is an average decrease of about 3% per year.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We encourage retailers to diversify their businesses to reduce their dependence on profits from sale of tobacco products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Yee Chia Hsing have spoken up strongly against second-hand smoke and asked if there is more that we can do to minimise their effects in housing estates.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MOH works with MEWR to minimise exposure to second-hand smoke in the community.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MOH's measures are aimed at reducing the number of smokers over time, while smoking prohibitions in public areas will protect non-smokers from the immediate harm of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We urge smokers to be socially responsible and considerate when smoking in private spaces so that their neighbours will not be affected.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Residents who are affected should approach their neighbours to resolve the matter amicably in the spirit of neighbourliness.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Residents can also approach the Community Mediation Centre for assistance.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah made some suggestions to enhance the enforcement of the smoking ban in public spaces.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I agree that we should work more closely with members of the public to tackle errant smokers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I will refer her suggestions to my MEWR colleagues for their consideration.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ultimately, by discouraging those below the age of 21 from smoking, this Bill helps to reduce the number of adult smokers in the population in the long run and will help reduce second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Alex Yam asked if we should ban tobacco completely since it is a major public health scourge.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We should not make the same mistake with ENDS.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We do not need nor want another addictive and harmful product to take root here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is why we are strengthening our regulatory measures against ENDS.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I believe I have responded to the main concerns of Members.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are grateful for the support of the public received during consultations and the support from this House.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: But, perhaps, if we could take the lead in this and set the standard for the international community and, perhaps, proceed on a ban at a far earlier stage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Opium use was quite entrenched in the early days in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: We bit the bullet and we introduced —

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: — a ban and we no longer have the problem.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Back to the point on the staggered system of introducing the increase in the age limit, can I ask the Parliamentary Secretary what exactly are the numbers that would be affected if we introduce an immediate ban?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I understand that it is hard to break the habit.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But that is something that we need to take into account.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is also to allow them some time to phase in because, as I have mentioned, smoking is an addiction.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, we are phasing in to allow them time to adjust.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is it the Ministry's view that all three studies seem to provide some initial grounds, even though they are not foolproof grounds, but some initial grounds that e-cigarettes, a controlled supply can be given to smokers?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is it the view of the Ministry that all three are methodologically flawed?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And, if so, in what manner is that the case?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Nevertheless, I would argue that that is a relevant question because, if there is evidence that e-cigarettes have reduced harm, then we should seriously consider that can be an option for smoking cessation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And, in this context, the Parliamentary Secretary cited an article in the Lancet.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The author of the Cochrane Report, Jamie Hartmann-Boyce, actually talked about some of the studies that his committee reviewed that purport to show that e-cigarettes prevent people from quitting, such as the one published in the Lancet − respiratory medicine which the Parliamentary Secretary cited from.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And he mentioned that some of these studies are flawed because they did not follow the research gold standard of randomised control trials.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: He said that, I quote, "The studies have found that —

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Yes, just 20 seconds. "The studies...that find that e-cigarettes stop people from quitting are not randomised controlled trials.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Instead, they surveyed smokers and asked if they are using e-cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Then, some months later, they asked the same people if they are still smoking." So, I would like to ask for that.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The last point is that I am heartened to hear that if new clinical evidence presents itself, the Ministry may review its position.
